newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS SEEN STEADY-UP, PORK BELLIES STEADY-LOWER.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS SEEN STEADY-UP, PORK BELLIES STEADY-LOWER.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to up 0.100 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were called to open steady to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover technical, and possibly commercial support, was expected in hog futures. Futures are discount to the lean hog index and cash hogs were seen ranging steady to firm in the western Corn Belt, analysts said.
However, further weakness in cash pork products, with cutout values quoted by USDA down $0.37 to $0.42 per cwt, and a seasonal trend for increased hog numbers, will limit gains, they added.

August pork belly futures were expected to show carryover pressure after closing limit down on Thursday. The break in the fresh belly market should keep pressure on that month despite lack of deliveries, analysts said.
Cash 16-18 lb fresh bellies declined to $84 per cwt and 14-16 lb bellies fell as low as $85 after trading up to $92 last week.
Next year contracts will likely continue to trade technically and prices were expected to remain near steady, they added.
